4.4 Magnitude Earthquake Jolts Delhi-NCR; Epicentre In Haryana's Jhajjar
Earthquake in Delhi Today: No casualties or damage have been reported so far, but authorities are closely monitoring the situation.
The epicentre was in Haryana. (File photo) The epicentre was in Haryana. (File photo)
A 4.4-magnitude earthquake struck Delhi-NCR on Thursday morning, with the epicentre located in Haryana’s Jhajjar, 51 km west of Delhi. According to the National Centre for Seismology, the tremor occurred at 9:04 AM IST at a depth of 10 km, with coordinates 28.63°N latitude and 76.68°E longitude.
In a post on X, Delhi Police said there have been no reports of damage so far after the earthquake.

“No reports of any damage have been received so far from the earthquake that struck Delhi NCR this morning. We pray for the well-being of all Delhi residents," said Delhi Police.

The sudden jolt startled residents across Delhi, Noida, Gurugram, and nearby areas. The brief but noticeable tremor prompted many people to rush out of their homes and offices in panic.
Tremors were also felt as far as Meerut and Shamli in western Uttar Pradesh, about 200 km from the epicentre in Jhajjar.
A man in Ghaziabad, UP said: “…I had woken up just at the time when there was a jolt. I was scared. There was another earthquake just a few days ago. Delhi-NCR experiences earthquakes quite often. So, we should be mindful of safety and precautions…"

Delhi-NCR, situated in India’s Seismic Zone IV, frequently experiences mild to moderate earthquakes. On February 17, 2025, a 4.0-magnitude earthquake struck near Dhaula Kuan in central Delhi at 5:36 AM. The tremor, originating at a shallow depth of 5 km, caused noticeable shaking across the region, prompting residents to evacuate buildings in alarm. While no significant damage was reported, the incident underscored the city’s vulnerability to seismic activity.
